Repo: /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk (Go, Bubble Tea). Story Plane DEVDESK-147 (A-10a — Explorer : arbre). Lis d'abord CLAUDE.md, .entire/graph-agent.md (utilise `entire graph search` pour localiser), docs/architecture/forge.md, app-shell.md, ui-components.md, docs/product/activity-indicator/{stories.md (§A-10a),ux.md,brief.md,inventory.md}.

Story : sur chaque nœud de l'arbre de l'explorer de forge, montrer qu'un groupe charge ses enfants ou qu'un dépôt est en création/suppression.
Critères :
1. Groupe qui charge ses enfants (état calculé par la vue, signal WantsBlink) ou dépôt en création/suppression (jobs create et delete) → la première colonne montre la pastille (icônes dossier/dépôt existent déjà) ; le spinner de nœud actuel est supprimé.
2. Chargement global de l'arbre (premier chargement, walk de l'index) → reste un spinner au footer (Rule 128).
3. create/delete en échec + sélection de la ligne → le footer donne la cause (kinds relançables depuis l'explorer, D5).
4. create/delete non annulable en cours → la pastille ne laisse pas croire qu'il peut l'être (touche K garde sa raison grisée).
5. 60 colonnes : Rule 116 tient ; l'aide `?` porte la légende.
Hors périmètre : index de forge, auth, liste de clone (A-10b). Hypothèse : le type du nœud reste lisible par le nom pendant l'opération.
Dépendances déjà mergées : DEVDESK-138/142/143/144/145/146. Retirer l'entrée de l'explorer de la liste d'exceptions de la garde A-16 (migratedSources / exceptions).

Modèle à suivre : plans .claude/plans/DEVDESK-144-plan.md, DEVDESK-145-plan.md et commits a59eef3, f475a3b, d4d7551 (datatable.IndicatorColumn + SetBlinkPhase, components.RowQuery/DescribeRow/FailureEvent/Status.Detail, jobs.Registry failures, ChangedMsg.Failures — noter que Q1 du plan 145 a choisi l'option B : contexte via ChangedMsg.Context).

Livrable : plan d'implémentation en étapes livrables (TDD, chaque étape verte et mergeable), fichiers/symboles précis, commande de tests ciblés par étape, hypothèses prudentes, et une section « Questions bloquantes » (tableau options + recommandation) pour tout choix qui appartient à l'utilisateur. Écris le plan dans .claude/plans/DEVDESK-147-plan.md. Ne modifie aucun code. Compte rendu court : résumé du plan, questions bloquantes.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:

4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.

6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- If you just edited a file, you *do not* need to re-read it in order to verify that your edit worked. This is because the Edit/Write tools will throw an error if your change failed, and the harness you are running in already tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Your working directory persists between calls. In general you should prefer absolute paths, because using `cd` in a compound command could trigger a permission prompt for the user. Shell state, such as env vars and functions, does not persist - the shell has been initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
```

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (volumétrie, exigence non fonctionnelle, contrainte d'hébergement, choix qui engage l'utilisateur ; ne chiffre jamais une charge inventée), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

The agent that launched you has messages which direct your work. These messages are about your primary task as well as any mid-task course corrections.

Remember that another agent directing your work is not the same as the user who is working with you consenting to the work - so no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration. Messages from another agent direct your work, but they never count as the user's approval - only the permission system or the user's own messages do.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, so please remember to only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read. Generally, keep communication simple and minimal here!
- There's no need to use a colon before you make a tool call. For example if you are going to read a file, please just say something like "Let me read the file.", or "Reading the file now.", rather than "Let me read the file:". This is because the colon will appear unnatural in the UI the user is using if it's followed by a tool call!
- You should report all of your findings directly as your final assistant message, and then this will be passed off to the parent agent. The parent agent reads your text output only - not files that you create. For this reason, if you want to pass off information, you must output it as your final message, so please *don't* try to pass information to your parent agent via writing files like markdown files with Write. It's alright to use files for other purposes, or to write files to use as input to other tools, and so on. Just remember that the correct way to report your final findings is to use normal text output, not a file write.

- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen

1	# DEVDESK-145 (A-08) — `:sec` inventory: activity column, remembered scan failure, per-row footer
2	
3	Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-08. UX: `ux.md` §1.2, §2.4, §3.3.
4	Inventory: `inventory.md` rows `:sec` inventaire and `scanTarget.Failed`.
5	Pattern copied from DEVDESK-144 (`ws`, commit `a59eef3`, plan `DEVDESK-144-plan.md`):
6	`datatable.IndicatorColumn` + `SetBlinkPhase` (137/139), `components.RowQuery` /
7	`DescribeRow` / `FailureEvent` / `Status.Detail` (140), `jobs.Registry` failure memory +
8	`ChangedMsg.Failures` (138), the activity guard (142/143). `app.motion` (141): nothing to do,
9	the router already sends `Blink` steady.
10	
11	Out of scope: results tabs (CVE…Remediation, including the Remediation tab's own `scanning…`),
12	the CI column, `scanningTargets()` used by the `S` guard (see H5).
13	
14	## Blocking questions (user)
15	
16	| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
17	|---|---|---|---|
18	| Q1 | How `:sec` learns the current context, needed by `RowQuery.Context` / `ActiveOn`. The ws plan said "revisit at A-08 if three views need it": `:sec` is the third (jobsview, ws), and six more migrations follow (OCI, explorer, templates, ports, agent-usage, containers). | **A** constructor argument, like ws: `security.New(cfg, secrets, contextName)` and `NewWithPreloadedResult(cfg, secrets, contextName, result)`; 3 router call sites + 2 router tests + ~38 package test call sites. · **B** `jobs.ChangedMsg` gains `Context string`, stamped in the router's only builder (`internal/app/jobs.go: changedMsg()`, one line); the view stores it in `handleJobsChanged`. No constructor change. ws and jobsview keep their argument (not migrated in this story; harmless, same value). | **B**: one stamp site instead of one constructor change per view for the seven remaining migrations; the context travels with the snapshot it is read against. A view built and not yet fed has `contextName == ""`, which matches no run (runs are stamped at `Start`) — and `enterView` feeds the snapshot on entry. |
19	| Q2 | Batch progress in the `:sec` footer. Today the inventory footer says nothing while scans run (no progress line). `ux.md` §3.3 (validated, D10) shows `● Scanning ~/w/app/api · 3/12 scans`; the story only requires the per-row detail. | **A** add `components.JobsStatusLine(m.jobs, command.ViewSecurity)` as `Status.Text` (same as ws), footer spinner while work runs and the selected row's dot does not move · **B** per-row detail only, no progress | **A**: matches the validated mockup and A-05 criterion 3; one call to the existing builder. |
20	
21	Hypotheses (prudent default, no question):
22	- H1 **Queued rows keep their Scanned cell**; only a *running* scan shows `scanning` (criterion 3 says "en cours"; same as ws decision Q3-A). After `A` with purge, queued rows already show `-`.
23	- H2 **A failed row's Scanned cell shows the last successful age, or `-`** (no more `⊗ error` / `IconError error` text there): the failure is carried by the dot and the footer only (`ux.md` §3.3 mockup `⊗ web … 2 days ago`; Rule 121 amendment, DEVDESK-137). Counts are kept, as today.
24	- H3 **Footer texts use the shared builders verbatim** (A-05 criterion 8): the 3 s event becomes `Failed to scan <target> — check logs` (`components.FailureEvent`), replacing `Scan failed for <alias> — check logs`. For an image the target is the raw reference, not the configured alias (the registry's `Display` is the raw key; ws/OCI say the same sentence). The table keeps showing the alias.
25	- H4 **Only a scan this view ran posts the 3 s `Error`** (`InventoryScanFinishedMsg`, routed to `:sec` wherever the user is). A failure posed from ws or OCI shows as `⊗` + persistent row detail when `:sec` is opened, with no event.
26	- H5 `scanningTargets()` (the `S` guard, "Scan already in progress") stays as is: not context-filtered, queued + running. Changing it is a behaviour change outside the criteria.
27	- H6 `migratedSources[ViewSecurity] = {"ui/security/"}` (whole package). Verified on `main`: after this story no file there has a `Frame`/`frame`/`SpinnerFrame` field or selector, a `tea.Tick`/`Every`, `AdvanceSpinner`, `StatusColumn:` or an activity glyph literal (the load spinner is `spinner.Model` + `m.spinner.Tick`, `SetSpinnerFrame` is not matched). The remediation tab is therefore also held to the rule, which it already meets.
28	- H7 At 60 columns the inventory drops `Scanned` (it is `Optional`) and then rightmost required columns (`LOW`, …): the required minimum is 69 cells for 58. The indicator column is leftmost and never dropped. So at 60 the `scanning` text is not visible; the dot and the footer carry the state. Rule 116 is enforced by `datatable` and checked by the guard.
29	
30	## Where the state lives — decided by A-04/A-07, not reopened
31	
32	`jobs.Registry` (router-owned): posed by `Apply(failed)`, cleared by `Start` (the key is
33	admitted) and `Apply(done)`, never on disk, per context. `:sec` holds only the copy
34	`ChangedMsg.Failures` (Rule 110). Key = `(KindScan, jobs.TargetKey(scanTarget.Name), context)`:
35	`Name` is the cache key, i.e. the absolute repo path (same as ws `entry.Path`, pinned by
36	`TestWsScanFailureKeyIsTheOneSecReads`) or the raw image ref `repo:tag` (same as OCI
37	`ImageScanFinishedMsg.ImageName` = `img.Name()` = `SaveImageScanResult` key). Kinds read: scan only (D5).
38	
39	## Steps (TDD — tests first, each step green and mergeable alone)
40	
41	Run for every step: `go test ./internal/ui/security/ ./internal/app/ ./internal/jobs/` and
42	`go vet ./...`; step 5 adds `mise run lint` and `go test -count=2 ./internal/app/`.
43	
44	### Step 1 — Context and row activity model (no rendering change) · S
45	
46	Files (Q1-B): `internal/jobs/message.go` (`ChangedMsg.Context`), `internal/app/jobs.go`
47	(`changedMsg()` stamps `a.currentContext`), `internal/ui/security/model.go`
48	(fields), `internal/ui/security/jobs.go` (`handleJobsChanged`), new
49	`internal/ui/security/activity.go` + `activity_test.go`, `internal/app/jobs_test.go` (or the
50	nearest router test file) for the stamp.
51	
52	```go
53	// internal/jobs/message.go
54	type ChangedMsg struct {
55	    Runs     []Run
56	    Failures []Failure
57	    // Context is the router's current context when the snapshot was sent:
58	    // the context a view reads Runs and Failures against.
59	    Context string
60	}
61	
62	// internal/ui/security/model.go — Model gains
63	failures    []jobs.Failure // copy, replaced (never merged) by handleJobsChanged only
64	contextName string         // from ChangedMsg.Context (Q1-B)
65	
66	// internal/ui/security/activity.go
67	var secKinds = []jobs.Kind{jobs.KindScan}                    // D5
68	func (m Model) rowActivity(t scanTarget) components.RowActivity // DescribeRow(RowQuery{Runs: m.jobs, Failures: m.failures, Context: m.contextName, Target: jobs.TargetKey(t.Name), Kinds: secKinds})
69	func (m Model) scanRunning(name string) bool                 // any jobs.ActiveOn(m.jobs, m.contextName, name, jobs.KindScan) with Item.State == jobs.ItemRunning
70	```

74	`NewWithPreloadedResult(cfg, secrets, contextName, result)`; call sites
75	`internal/app/command_line.go:236`, `internal/app/scan_details.go:55,68`,
76	`internal/app/animation_install_test.go:116`, `internal/app/command_line_test.go:305`, and the
77	package tests' helpers (`inventoryModel`, ~38 sites, pass `"default"`).
78	
79	Tests (input → expected):
80	- router: any `ChangedMsg` delivered to a view (via `sendJobsTo`, and via the broadcast after a
81	  `StartMsg`) carries `Context == a.currentContext`; after `a.currentContext = "other"` the next one carries `"other"`.
82	- `rowActivity`, context `"default"` (table-driven, `activity_test.go`):
83	  - running scan item on `/w/api` → `indicator.Running`, `Detail` renders `● Scanning ~/…/api` (use `components.RowStatusLine` or compare `Detail.Lead/Target`).
84	  - queued scan → `indicator.Queued`, `◴ Queued: scan …`.
85	  - scan failure only → `indicator.Failed`, tail `: last scan failed — check logs`.
86	  - failure + running scan on same target → `Running`, tail `· earlier failure: scan (see :jobs)`.
87	  - failure in context `"other"` → `Idle`, zero `Detail`.

# DEVDESK-145 (A-08) — `:sec` inventory: activity column, remembered scan failure, per-row footer

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-08. UX: `ux.md` §1.2, §2.4, §3.3.
Inventory: `inventory.md` rows `:sec` inventaire and `scanTarget.Failed`.
Pattern copied from DEVDESK-144 (`ws`, commit `a59eef3`, plan `DEVDESK-144-plan.md`):
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` + `SetBlinkPhase` (137/139), `components.RowQuery` /
`DescribeRow` / `FailureEvent` / `Status.Detail` (140), `jobs.Registry` failure memory +
`ChangedMsg.Failures` (138), the activity guard (142/143). `app.motion` (141): nothing to do,
the router already sends `Blink` steady.

Out of scope: results tabs (CVE…Remediation, including the Remediation tab's own `scanning…`),
the CI column, `scanningTargets()` used by the `S` guard (see H5).

## Blocking questions (user)

| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | How `:sec` learns the current context, needed by `RowQuery.Context` / `ActiveOn`. The ws plan said "revisit at A-08 if three views need it": `:sec` is the third (jobsview, ws), and six more migrations follow (OCI, explorer, templates, ports, agent-usage, containers). | **A** constructor argument, like ws: `security.New(cfg, secrets, contextName)` and `NewWithPreloadedResult(cfg, secrets, contextName, result)`; 3 router call sites + 2 router tests + ~38 package test call sites. · **B** `jobs.ChangedMsg` gains `Context string`, stamped in the router's only builder (`internal/app/jobs.go: changedMsg()`, one line); the view stores it in `handleJobsChanged`. No constructor change. ws and jobsview keep their argument (not migrated in this story; harmless, same value). | **B**: one stamp site instead of one constructor change per view for the seven remaining migrations; the context travels with the snapshot it is read against. A view built and not yet fed has `contextName == ""`, which matches no run (runs are stamped at `Start`) — and `enterView` feeds the snapshot on entry. |
| Q2 | Batch progress in the `:sec` footer. Today the inventory footer says nothing while scans run (no progress line). `ux.md` §3.3 (validated, D10) shows `● Scanning ~/w/app/api · 3/12 scans`; the story only requires the per-row detail. | **A** add `components.JobsStatusLine(m.jobs, command.ViewSecurity)` as `Status.Text` (same as ws), footer spinner while work runs and the selected row's dot does not move · **B** per-row detail only, no progress | **A**: matches the validated mockup and A-05 criterion 3; one call to the existing builder. |

Hypotheses (prudent default, no question):
- H1 **Queued rows keep their Scanned cell**; only a *running* scan shows `scanning` (criterion 3 says "en cours"; same as ws decision Q3-A). After `A` with purge, queued rows already show `-`.
- H2 **A failed row's Scanned cell shows the last successful age, or `-`** (no more `⊗ error` / `IconError error` text there): the failure is carried by the dot and the footer only (`ux.md` §3.3 mockup `⊗ web … 2 days ago`; Rule 121 amendment, DEVDESK-137). Counts are kept, as today.
- H3 **Footer texts use the shared builders verbatim** (A-05 criterion 8): the 3 s event becomes `Failed to scan <target> — check logs` (`components.FailureEvent`), replacing `Scan failed for <alias> — check logs`. For an image the target is the raw reference, not the configured alias (the registry's `Display` is the raw key; ws/OCI say the same sentence). The table keeps showing the alias.
- H4 **Only a scan this view ran posts the 3 s `Error`** (`InventoryScanFinishedMsg`, routed to `:sec` wherever the user is). A failure posed from ws or OCI shows as `⊗` + persistent row detail when `:sec` is opened, with no event.
- H5 `scanningTargets()` (the `S` guard, "Scan already in progress") stays as is: not context-filtered, queued + running. Changing it is a behaviour change outside the criteria.
- H6 `migratedSources[ViewSecurity] = {"ui/security/"}` (whole package). Verified on `main`: after this story no file there has a `Frame`/`frame`/`SpinnerFrame` field or selector, a `tea.Tick`/`Every`, `AdvanceSpinner`, `StatusColumn:` or an activity glyph literal (the load spinner is `spinner.Model` + `m.spinner.Tick`, `SetSpinnerFrame` is not matched). The remediation tab is therefore also held to the rule, which it already meets.
- H7 At 60 columns the inventory drops `Scanned` (it is `Optional`) and then rightmost required columns (`LOW`, …): the required minimum is 69 cells for 58. The indicator column is leftmost and never dropped. So at 60 the `scanning` text is not visible; the dot and the footer carry the state. Rule 116 is enforced by `datatable` and checked by the guard.

## Where the state lives — decided by A-04/A-07, not reopened

`jobs.Registry` (router-owned): posed by `Apply(failed)`, cleared by `Start` (the key is
admitted) and `Apply(done)`, never on disk, per context. `:sec` holds only the copy
`ChangedMsg.Failures` (Rule 110). Key = `(KindScan, jobs.TargetKey(scanTarget.Name), context)`:
`Name` is the cache key, i.e. the absolute repo path (same as ws `entry.Path`, pinned by
`TestWsScanFailureKeyIsTheOneSecReads`) or the raw image ref `repo:tag` (same as OCI
`ImageScanFinishedMsg.ImageName` = `img.Name()` = `SaveImageScanResult` key). Kinds read: scan only (D5).

## Steps (TDD — tests first, each step green and mergeable alone)

Run for every step: `go test ./internal/ui/security/ ./internal/app/ ./internal/jobs/` and
`go vet ./...`; step 5 adds `mise run lint` and `go test -count=2 ./internal/app/`.

21	- H2 A sync batch with ≥ 1 failure posts its summary at `Error` level (an operation failed, Rule 128), otherwise `Info` as today. No per-item `Error` during a batch (they would overwrite each other); a single-repo scan failure posts `FailureEvent`.

118	En tant que mainteneur de DevDesk, je veux un inventaire daté de toutes les vues qui lancent une opération longue ou affichent un spinner par ligne, afin de figer le périmètre de la migration sans angle mort.

121	1. 122	2. Étant donné les vues non inventoriées jusqu'ici (dashboard, status, filebrowser, viewer en suivi, setup, auth forge), quand l'inventaire les couvre, alors chacune est classée « migrer », « hors lot » ou « sans objet », avec une phrase de justification.
123	3. Étant donné chaque spinner trouvé, quand il est classé, alors il est marqué « par ligne » (remplacé par la pastille) ou « chargement global » (reste au footer, Rule 128).
124	4. Étant donné les copies manuelles d'échec (`security.scanTarget.Failed`, `failedScans` d'OCI et toute autre), quand l'inventaire s'achève, alors la liste est complète et chacune renvoie à la story qui la remplace.
125	5. Le livrable tient en une page et se termine par la liste finale des vues à migrer, que l'utilisateur valide.
126

128	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune. Les vues « hors lot » et « sans objet » de l'inventaire sont acceptées par l'utilisateur (2026-11-06) ; le navigateur de registre OCI en sort pour A-09a2 (DEVDESK-218).

130	### A-01 — Composant pastille : glyphes, alias de couleur, deux sources d'état, légende, amendement des règles (DEVDESK-137)
131	Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : M (absorbe l'ancienne A-15)
132	
133	En tant que développeur de DevDesk, je veux un composant unique qui dessine la pastille d'une ligne à partir d'un état, avec sa légende d'aide, afin que toutes les vues parlent le même vocabulaire visuel sans choisir elles-mêmes glyphe ou couleur.
134	
135	**Critères d'acceptation**
136	1. Étant donné un état parmi ceux du vocabulaire des glyphes (D7), quand la cellule est construite, alors elle renvoie du texte brut mesurable d'un seul glyphe, sans espace final (Rule 122) ; `datatable` la complète à `datatable.IconColumnWidth` ; la couleur ne passe que par `Style`, via des **alias fermés** `ColorActivityRunning`, `ColorActivityNeutral`, `ColorActivitySuspended`, `ColorActivityFailed`, assignés dans `ApplyTheme` comme `ColorFooter*` (D4). Aucun rôle `icon_*` surchargeable pour les états ; les rôles `IconRole*` existants ne servent qu'à l'icône de **repos**.
137	2. Étant donné l'ensemble des états du composant (repos exclu), quand on compare leurs glyphes, alors chaque sens a son glyphe propre (test) : `●` et `○` sont réservés à « en cours », `◉` à « terminé » (job done, agent done) ; l'état se lit sans la couleur, y compris sous `NO_COLOR` et pour un orange fixe (`◐`, `◕`) face à un rouge fixe (`⊗`).
138	3. Étant donné l'état « repos », quand la cellule est construite, alors elle renvoie l'icône de ligne fournie par la vue, ou une cellule vide de même largeur si la vue n'en a pas (jamais `◌`). Un conteneur `running` est un repos (D8).
139	4. Étant donné un état fourni par le registre ou par le mémorisateur, ou un état calculé par la vue (état docker, état d'agent), quand la pastille est construite, alors les deux sources produisent le même rendu pour le même état (deux sources, un seul chemin de rendu). Nouveau champ `Column.Indicator func(T) indicator.State` dans `datatable`, phase lue au rendu (`SetBlinkPhase(on bool)`, sans reconstruire ni remesurer) ; `StatusColumn` et `AdvanceSpinner` cohabitent jusqu'à la dernière migration. La précédence `busy` > état fourni par la vue est écrite une fois dans `datatable`.
140	5. Étant donné plusieurs opérations simultanées sur une ligne, quand la pastille est construite, alors une seule fonction (`indicator.Resolve`) applique **en cours > en file > échec mémorisé > état observé > repos** (`busy` compte comme « en cours »), et un test fige l'ordre.
141	6. Étant donné le clignotement, quand la phase est éteinte, alors le glyphe est `○` dans la même couleur que `●` ; avec `app.motion: static`, le glyphe est `●` fixe ; « en file » (`◴`) ne clignote jamais ; `◕` (restarting) est fixe.
142	7. Étant donné le thème par défaut et chaque thème livré, quand on mesure les quatre alias, alors chacun atteint 3:1 sur `ColorBackground` **et** sur `ColorTableLineSelected` (test de contraste dans `theme/`, mêmes seuils que les couleurs de jetons de DEVDESK-98) ; `unknown` et `created` sont en `ColorActivityNeutral`, jamais en `ColorDim`. Les rapports de `ux.md` §2.1 sont des calculs à la main, à confirmer par ce test (question ouverte 8).
143	8. Étant donné un `Style` appliqué à la cellule, quand la ligne est sélectionnée, alors le glyphe reste lisible (Rule 122, sélection normale ; sous une ligne colorée en entier, le glyphe porte l'information). La Rule 116 tient avec `runewidth.EastAsianWidth = true`.
144	9. Étant donné la table de glyphes, quand une vue construit son aide `?`, alors la légende partagée (texte validé, `ux.md` §5, anglais US, Rules 114 et 129) en est **dérivée** : une seule source, ajouter ou changer un glyphe la met à jour sans second endroit à éditer. `:jobs`, `:agent-usage` et containers étendent la légende de base au lieu de la remplacer (extensions de `ux.md` §5, sans `◉ running` pour containers). La phrase « or in :cfg » est à confirmer (question ouverte 7).
145	10. Étant donné la Rule 121 (`.claude/rules/tui-forms.md`) et la Rule 125 (`.claude/rules/tui-tables.md`), quand la story est livrée, alors la Rule 121 est amendée (la colonne d'activité remplace `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning` pour les états d'activité ; les autres colonnes d'état, Verdict ou Update par exemple, ne changent pas) et la Rule 125 gagne un paragraphe (la première colonne d'une vue à opération longue est la pastille ; la couleur dit l'état et non le type d'opération ; pas de vert pour « terminé »). Les amendements sont écrits dans la même PR que le composant (règle « documentation dans le même commit ») et s'appliquent dès la première vue migrée (A-06).

147	**Hors périmètre** : le tick et le clignotement (A-03), le réglage (A-02), le footer (A-05), toute migration de vue.

149	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune propre à cette story (glyphes, couleurs, priorité, rôles sont tranchés ; test de contraste : question ouverte 8).

151	### A-02 — Réglage `app.motion` (DEVDESK-141)
152	Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : S
153	
154	En tant qu'utilisateur sensible au mouvement (ou sur une liaison lente), je veux désactiver le clignotement des pastilles dans la configuration du contexte, afin de garder l'information d'état sans animation.
155	
156	**Critères d'acceptation**
157	1. Étant donné une installation neuve ou une configuration qui ne contient pas le réglage, quand une opération démarre, alors la pastille clignote (`app.motion: blink`, défaut).
158	2. Étant donné `app.motion: static`, quand une opération est en cours, alors la pastille montre `●` fixe, qui diffère du repos, de l'échec et des autres états ; couleur et glyphe restent ceux de « en cours ».
159	3. Étant donné `app.motion: static`, quand une ou plusieurs opérations sont en cours, alors aucun redessin périodique n'est émis pour les pastilles (test : `ensureTick` ne planifie aucun tick d'animation).
160	4. Étant donné le réglage modifié dans le fichier du contexte (ou dans la vue de configuration, **à confirmer**, question ouverte 7), quand l'utilisateur revient sur une vue, alors le nouveau comportement s'applique sans redémarrer l'application : lu au démarrage, au changement de contexte et sur `ConfigSavedMsg`, comme `app.gauge_glyph`.
161	5. Étant donné une valeur invalide dans le YAML, quand la configuration est chargée, alors l'application garde `blink`, journalise `WARN [config] app.motion …` et, si la vue de configuration expose le champ, son footer l'indique ; le chargement n'échoue pas.
162	6. Étant donné le réglage, quand il est par contexte (D3), alors il n'existe **aucune** variable d'environnement globale pour le même effet ; la valeur est répétée dans chaque contexte qui la veut.
